name: Nasi Lemak
description: Fragrant coconut rice served with spicy sambal, crispy anchovies, peanuts, cucumber and boiled eggs.
steps: Rinse rice and cook with coconut milk, water, pandan leaves and a pinch of salt until fluffy.
Boil eggs for 9–10 minutes, peel and cut in half.
Fry dried anchovies until crispy and golden.
Prepare or heat the sambal in a small pan.
Serve coconut rice with sambal, eggs, cucumber, anchovies and peanuts.

name: Nasi Ayam
description: Tender chicken with fragrant garlic and ginger rice, served with cucumber and spicy chilli sauce.
steps: Season chicken with salt and pepper, then simmer in water until fully cooked.
Remove chicken and reserve the cooking broth as chicken stock.
Saute garlic and ginger in sesame oil, then add washed rice and chicken stock.
Cook rice until fluffy and fragrant.
Brush chicken with soy sauce and serve with rice, cucumber and chilli sauce.

name: Char Kuey Teow
description: Smoky stir-fried flat rice noodles with prawns, eggs, bean sprouts and savoury sauces.
steps: Heat cooking oil in a wok over high heat and saute garlic until fragrant.
Add prawns and stir-fry until cooked through.
Push prawns aside, crack in eggs and scramble lightly.
Add flat rice noodles, soy sauces and chilli paste, tossing quickly.
Add bean sprouts and Chinese chives, stir-fry briefly and serve hot.

name: Kuih Seri Muka
description: A traditional two-layer Malaysian kuih combining soft coconut glutinous rice with smooth pandan custard.
ingredients: 200 g glutinous rice, soaked for 3 hours
150 ml coconut milk for rice layer
steps: Drain soaked glutinous rice and mix with coconut milk, water and salt.
Steam rice for 25–30 minutes until tender, then press firmly into a greased square pan.
Whisk eggs, coconut milk, pandan juice, sugar and flour until smooth, then strain.
Pour pandan custard over the rice layer and steam gently for 25–30 minutes until set.
Cool completely before slicing into neat squares.

name: Cucur Udang
description: Crispy golden prawn fritters packed with fresh vegetables and served with sweet chilli sauce.
steps: Combine flour, turmeric powder and salt in a mixing bowl.
Add egg and water gradually, stirring until a thick batter forms.
Fold in prawns, bean sprouts, carrot and spring onions.
Heat cooking oil and carefully drop spoonfuls of batter into the pan.
Fry until golden brown and cooked through, then drain and serve with chilli sauce.

name: Teh Tarik
description: Malaysia's iconic pulled milk tea, known for its rich flavour, creamy sweetness and frothy top.
steps: Bring water to a boil and steep black tea leaves for 4–5 minutes.
Strain the brewed tea into a heat-resistant jug.
Add condensed milk and evaporated milk, then stir until combined.
Carefully pour tea back and forth between two heat-resistant jugs to create a frothy texture.
Serve immediately while hot.
